evidence.note: CONFIRMED. Claim: ddflow decide derives its default doc path from the decision id slug, not the task globs, so a decide task globbing docs/ddflow/decisions/answers.md is refused. Probing test: test_decide_defaults_to_a_doc_the_task_globs_name (new). Ran on unfixed code: uv run pytest -q tests/test_decide_verb.py::test_decide_defaults_to_a_doc_the_task_globs_name -> 'docs/ddflow/decisions/x.md is outside X-decide's globs' (exit 3). Mechanism read in ddflow/api/decide.py: rel = path or f'{DOC_DIR}/{slug_of(decision_id)}.md'.

Bug fix task fix-B502b06b881; globs cover the changed files (tests/test_decide_verb.py, ddflow/api/decide.py, ddflow/surfaces/declared/decide.py). Rules read: r-gemini-key-load (export GEMINI_API_KEY before review), r-task-phase-needs-wave. No applicable rule contradicts the change.

Implemented --append/--body and default-path-from-globs in ddflow/api/decide.py + ddflow/surfaces/declared/decide.py; 3 regression tests added to tests/test_decide_verb.py. ruff check + ruff format --check clean on all 3 files.

chunk_findings.detail: `_default_rel` returns the first `it.globs` entry that merely starts with `DOC_DIR/` and ends in `.md`, and `decide` then writes that string as a file path. Given globs `["docs/ddflow/decisions/*.md"]` (the shape `inside()` exists to accept), the default used to be `docs/ddflow/decisions/<slug>.md`, which matches the pattern; it is now the pattern itself, so the write is either refused by `inside` or creates a file named `*.md`. The same first-match rule also lands on the wrong file when the task names two docs, e.g. `["docs/ddflow/decisions/notes.md", "docs/ddflow/decisions/answers.md"]` with decision id `D-x`: the body is written to `notes.md`, not `answers.md`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decide.py:_default_rel

chunk_findings.detail: `--append` is not idempotent. `replace_text` runs before `W.commit` and completion. If the commit fails (hook, or any error other than "nothing to commit") and the operator retries `decide --append --body "Q: left open?\nA: settled now."` on the same claimed item, `target.exists()` is already true and the previous render-plus-body is concatenated again. The landed doc then contains the decision restatement and the Q-and-A twice. The old replace path rewrote the same bytes; this path cannot.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decide.py:decide

chunk_findings.detail: The path parameter still advertises `default docs/ddflow/decisions/<slug>.md`. After this change, a task globbed to `docs/ddflow/decisions/answers.md` with `--decision-id D-x` and no `--path` writes `answers.md`, not `x.md`. The flag help states a default the code no longer uses.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/decide.py:path

chunk_findings.detail: The append test only checks that the pre-existing proposal sentence and the `--body` Q-and-A appear in `HEAD:docs/ddflow/decisions/x.md`. It never asserts the restated decision (`render` output: status, title, or decision text). A regression that prepends the old file and appends `body` while dropping `render` still passes, so the test does not lock the behavior the docstring promises.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_decide_verb.py:test_decide_keeps_an_existing_doc_and_appends_the_body

chunk_findings.detail: The test never runs `decide`, never claims an item, and never retries a failed commit. It only asserts `_append_block(block, block) == block` on two strings. A `decide --append` path that still calls `replace_text` with a fresh concatenation before `W.commit` — the retry that writes the restatement and Q-and-A twice when the hook rejects the first commit — leaves this test green. The name and comment promise idempotent retry; the assertions do not lock that path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_decide_verb.py:test_decide_appending_is_idempotent_on_a_retry

chunk_findings.detail:
`_append_block` treats “already written” as an unanchored substring check (`block.strip() in existing`), so a later `--append` whose new block is a prefix of what a failed commit already left on disk is dropped and the stale text is what gets committed. First call with `--body "Answer one. Answer two is longer."` writes `render + "

" + that sentence` and `W.commit` fails; a retry with the corrected shorter body `"Answer one."` builds `block2 = render + "

" + "Answer one.
"`, `block2.strip()` is a prefix of the file, and the function returns the file unchanged — the wrong longer body stays, `replace_text` rewrites it, and a commit that now succeeds lands the rejected wording.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/decide.py:_append_block
